messages:
Maria (runtime): heads-up - after the 5/14 deploy I'm seeing a sizeable latency spike on streaming endpoints. p50 up ~30ms, p95 up ~180ms for small prompts. CI perf job failed too, so rollout is paused :warning:
Aj (infra): thanks, pinging the rollout. Which deploy? can you paste the deploy id? :eyes:
Maria (runtime): deploy id: deploy/2026-05-14-03, PR#3421 (protocol-framing change). CI perf job: perf/streaming/178c7b failed with +25% tail latency. Logs attached below:
```log
STREAM: initial-chunk 220ms (was 20ms)
SSE: flush window=150ms (config change from 20ms)
ToolCall: serialization CPU spike 85% on worker-7
KVCache: miss-rate x4 on short-prefetch keys
```
Kevin (eng): oof. That flush window change was intentional to reduce small-packet overhead, but it explains the initial token delay. Did PR#3421 also change tool-call envelope serialization?
Maria (runtime): yes, it added an intermediate envelope and a synchronous JSON.stringify pass for tool-call metadata before handing to the runtime. I think that's where the CPU/serialization spike comes from.
Sarah (qa): I repro locally with small prompts. If I set SSE_FLUSH_MS back to 20, p50/p95 go back to baseline. Quick patch to env makes perf look normal.
Aj (infra): can we hotfix by reverting the SSE flush default and roll forward the rest? What's the risk?
Kevin (eng): low risk revert for the config change. But the double-serialize in tool-call might still add overhead even if we flush sooner. We should bisect the PR to separate framing vs tool-call changes.
Maria (runtime): I started a bisect: suspect commits in PR#3421: commits a1a2 -> b3b4 -> c5c6. Early sign points to commit b3b4 which introduced the envelope.
deploy-bot: Deployment halted for deploy/2026-05-14-03 (manual rollback required) :no_entry:
Aj (infra): i'll stage a revert of the SSE flush change now (fast path). Kevin, can you and Maria run a microbenchmark for serialization overhead? simple loop invoking tool-call with 1-2 small args.
Kevin (eng): on it. quick script I used:
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do node perf/toolcall-stub.js --serialize; done
```
Kevin (eng): initial run shows ~2.1ms/iter with envelope vs 0.15ms without. That's ~14x serialization overhead for tiny payloads. Not good.
Maria (runtime): KV cache miss increase might be secondary: the envelope changed cache key shape -> more misses for prefix cache. That plus SSE buffering multiplies the latency.
Sarah (qa): noted: KV key normalization landed in the same PR too. So we have three orthogonal changes folded into one PR: framing, serialization envelope, kv-key tweak. That's why rollout hit perf.
Aj (infra): plan: 1) revert SSE flush default immediately (low risk) 2) revert kv-key normalization until we roll a normalized key migration 3) leave envelope change queued for a targeted perf fix (avoid rolling back complex logic) 4) re-run CI perf after each revert.
Maria (runtime): +1. I'll prepare rollback patches for 1 & 2. Kevin - can you profile the serializer and propose a faster path (streaming stringify or native buffer assembly)?
Kevin (eng): yes, options: a) avoid double-stringify by passing structured metadata through runtime (binary envelope), b) use a fast C++ binding for small JSONs, c) precompute static metadata buffer for common cases. I'll spike (a) first.
Sarah (qa): I'll re-run end-to-end and perf CI after each revert. If we get green, we can unpause rollout.
Aj (infra): rolling back SSE flush now. Patch: revert commit 7f9e3 (SSE flush change). Pushing to canary pool.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: deploy/2026-05-14-03-revert-sse (canary) :rocket:
Maria (runtime): monitoring streams now. early signs: initial-chunk latency back to ~18ms. p95 dropping.
Kevin (eng): serializer spike still visible in CPU profile but overall tail is much better with flush revert. Will continue with serializer spike fix today.
Sarah (qa): CI perf re-run queued (job perf/streaming/178c7b-rerun).
Aj (infra): good job triaging — note for postmortem: avoid bundling framing + key normalization + serialization changes in the same PR. Smaller change sets would have isolated this earlier.
Maria (runtime): agreed. I'll open a short postmortem draft once things are stable. Thanks all. :clap:
